correctness.rationale: The proof uses a radial Rayleigh trial yielding (n+1) mean spoke conductance and two orthogonal first rim Fourier vectors whose averaged Rayleigh quotient is mean spoke plus mu_n times mean rim conductance. Their sharp one-dimensional affine max-min upper bound yields the three cost regimes. Complete uniform wheel Fourier eigenvalues give attainment. At ANY optimum both sine and cosine Rayleigh quotients are tight at lambda_2, hence these vectors are eigenvectors; the imaginary part of the complex rim Fourier eigenvector equation forces all rim conductances equal for n>=4, and the real part forces all spoke conductances equal. This covers nonnegative boundaries and exact equality price and proves global optimizer completeness. Taylor expansion gives T_n quadratic scaling. Actual standalone checker path check_wheel.py executed with VERIFY_OK 1246, including 4 rational eigenspectra, 2 rational Rayleigh identities and 1200 budget-feasible asymmetric competitors; finite checks are supplementary only.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Combining existing Laplacian eigenvalues with symmetry and a fresh one-dimensional max-min computation can recover the symmetric candidate, but that derivation is not an already stated implication giving the complete set of all edgewise optimizers. For an arbitrary non-symmetric optimum, saturation of both orthogonal Fourier Rayleigh tests and the imaginary parts of the eigenvector equations rule out each possible asymmetric rim weight. This critical structural step is not supplied by a generic spectral table or by a mere existence-of-symmetric-optimum theorem. The exact price threshold and critical continuum consequently remain the claim under assessment. The risk of an unlocated stronger paper remains explicitly open.

originality.rationale: Originality is the exact continuous-time wheel price frontier, all classwise conductance formulas, the complete critical optimal face and global non-asymmetric rigidity, not the general SDP or wheel Fourier spectrum. The closest exact wheel source Boyd et al. 2009 Section 5.4.3 solves a different discrete-time SLEM problem without arbitrary spoke cost; Sun et al. 2006 defines the continuous-time general SDP but lacks the specialized classification; Shafi et al. 2012 gives general spectral constraints. Searches of published records, primary full text, and wheel optimization aliases found no statement dominating the entire claim. Related wheel resistance work addresses the Kirchhoff index rather than lambda_2; no independence from unpublished work claimed. Residual risk of overlooked equivalent literature acknowledged.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family of hub-and-cycle communication networks receives a complete exact conductance purchasing rule under relative prices, not a finite artificial slice. The optimal topology changes at a sharp quadratic-in-size price threshold, with all rim edges deleted for fixed finite spoke price in sufficiently large wheels. The theorem resolves all optimal edgewise allocations, including degeneracy at the transition, and supplies analytic design without solving an SDP separately for each size or price. The rigidity proof and nonlinear size scaling make this more than a textbook spectral-table substitution. No claim of paper-sized contribution, downstream theorem, or arbitrary-network applicability is required.
